newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils develop their understanding of fractions by learning about unit fractions, non-unit fractions, fractions of shapes and groups, and how fractions combine to make a whole.

This lesson includes:
✔ Recognising halves, quarters and other fractions in shapes and groups
✔ Understanding that fractions must divide a whole into equal parts
✔ Identifying the numerator and denominator and explaining what each tells us
✔ Reading and writing unit fractions such as one half, one third, one fifth and one tenth
✔ Recognising that unit fractions always have a numerator of one
✔ Finding unit fractions of shapes and groups of objects
✔ Dividing groups into equal fractional parts
✔ Checking whether groups have been divided correctly into equal fractions
✔ Recognising and correcting mistakes involving numerators and denominators
✔ Understanding non-unit fractions and recognising that their numerator is greater than one
✔ Reading and writing non-unit fractions such as two thirds, three fifths and seven tenths
✔ Finding non-unit fractions of shapes and groups
✔ Finding a fraction of a quantity, such as three quarters of twelve
✔ Understanding how complementary fractions combine to make one whole
✔ Solving missing-whole problems from a known fractional part

Pupils begin by revisiting familiar fractions such as one half and one quarter before learning how the numerator and denominator describe equal parts of a whole. They then practise identifying and writing unit fractions in shapes and groups.

The lesson develops into non-unit fractions, where pupils use the denominator to identify how many equal parts make the whole and the numerator to count how many parts are selected. They apply this to rectangles, circles and groups of objects.

Later activities ask pupils to find fractions of quantities, check whether grouped objects correctly represent a given fraction, and explain common fraction mistakes.

The final section shows how fractions with the same denominator can combine to make one whole, and includes a challenge in which pupils work backwards from one half to find the total amount.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to identify, read and write unit and non-unit fractions, find fractions of shapes and quantities, and explain how fractions relate to one whole.
